question: What are the pieces of an OCI/Docker image (index, manifest, config, layers), and how does minibox walk from 'alpine:3.20' to a rootfs directory?
answer_hinglish:
Ek image ek single file nahi hai, yeh JSON documents aur tarballs ka ek chhota graph hai jo digests se jude hain.

1) INDEX (multi-arch list): media type application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json ya Docker ka manifest.list.v2+json. Isme har platform (linux/amd64, linux/arm64 v8, linux/arm v7...) ke liye ek manifest ka digest hota hai. Docker Hub alpine:3.20 ke liye index hi deta hai.
2) MANIFEST (ek platform ka): ek config descriptor aur layers ki list, har ek ka mediaType, digest aur size.
3) CONFIG blob: JSON jisme architecture, os, Env/Cmd waghera aur sabse important rootfs.diff_ids -- har layer ke UNCOMPRESSED tar ka sha256.
4) LAYERS: tar ya tar+gzip blobs, har ek us layer ki added/changed files aur deletions (whiteouts).

minibox/registry.py ka pull() exactly yahi chain chalata hai: reg.manifest('3.20') -> agar media INDEX_TYPES mein hai ya doc mein 'manifests' key hai, toh select_platform se apna platform chuno aur woh manifest BY DIGEST fetch karo -> config blob -> har layer blob -> sab verify -> phir image.apply_layer se dest/rootfs mein flatten. Saath mein dest/manifest.json aur dest/config.json bhi likhe jaate hain. Server par alpine:3.20 arm64 ka result: 1 layer, 4092319 bytes compressed, 517 tar entries, lagbhag 4 s. Note: config download hota hai lekin uske Env/Cmd/WorkingDir/User use NAHI hote -- command aap khud dete ho.
why_needed: Image ka model samjhe bina pull, verification ya caching kuch design nahi kar sakte -- har step kisi digest par tika hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek book series: index ek catalogue hai (Hindi edition, English edition), manifest ek edition ki table of contents, config uska preface jo chapters ke checksums list karta hai, aur layers asli chapters.
how_it_works: Tag -> index (platform list) -> platform manifest (by digest) -> config (by digest, diff_ids) -> layers (by digest). Har arrow ek sha256 digest hai, isliye har kadam verify ho sakta hai.
in_this_project: registry.py ke upar module docstring mein yeh 6 steps likhe hain. INDEX_TYPES, MANIFEST_TYPES, GZIP_LAYER_TYPES, PLAIN_LAYER_TYPES constants media types define karte hain. tests/unit/test_registry.py ka FakeRegistry yahi graph (index -> manifest -> config -> 2 gzip layers) memory mein banata hai.
code_example:
# real, minibox/registry.py pull (trimmed)
doc, media, mdigest = reg.manifest(ref.ref)
if media in INDEX_TYPES or "manifests" in doc:
    index_digest = mdigest
    chosen = select_platform(doc, os_name, arch, variant)
    doc, media, mdigest = reg.manifest(chosen["digest"])
if media not in MANIFEST_TYPES:
    raise RegistryError(f"unsupported manifest media type {media!r}")
advantages: Har cheez digest se named hai, isliye verify ho sakti hai
Ek tag ke peeche kai platforms
Layers images ke beech share ho sakti hain (minibox yeh nahi karta)
disadvantages: Ek image ke liye kai HTTP round trips
Media types ke do families (OCI aur Docker) dono handle karne padte hain
common_mistakes: Sochna ki tag seedha ek tarball hai
Config ko optional samajhna -- diff_ids wahi hai
Index aur manifest mein farak na karna

minibox image config ke Env/Cmd kyun ignore karta hai, aur use karna ho toh kahan jodoge?

question: What does 'content addressing' mean for container images, and what is the one function in minibox that every verification step goes through?
answer_hinglish:
Content addressing ka matlab: kisi cheez ka NAAM uske content ka hash hai. Blob ka naam sha256:<64 hex> hai, jo us blob ke exact bytes ka SHA-256 hai. Isliye 'yeh blob sahi hai ya nahi' ka sawal simple ho jaata hai: bytes ka hash nikalo aur naam se compare karo. Koi signature, koi trust nahi chahiye -- agar hash match, toh yahi woh bytes hain jo naam bolta hai.

minibox mein yeh image.check_digest(actual, expected, what) mein hai. Pehle expected ka format check hota hai: algo 'sha256' hona chahiye aur hex part exactly 64 chars -- warna DigestMismatch('unsupported or malformed digest'). Phir actual != expected toh DigestMismatch('digest mismatch: expected ..., got ...'). Hash do helpers se banta hai: sha256_bytes (manifest jaise chhote bodies ke liye) aur sha256_file (blobs ke liye, 1 MiB CHUNK mein stream karke, poori file memory mein nahi). sha256_file(path, gunzip=True) DECOMPRESSED stream ka hash deta hai, jo OCI diff_id hai.

Unit tests: test_check_digest_ok_and_mismatch, test_check_digest_rejects_malformed_expected ('md5:abc', 'sha256:short', 'sha256', '' sab reject), test_sha256_file_and_bytes_agree. Malformed expected ko reject karna zaroori hai: warna ek khali ya ajeeb digest string 'kuch bhi match' jaisa bug ban sakta tha.
why_needed: Network (registry, CDN, proxy) par bharosa kiye bina pakka karna ki jo bytes aaye woh wahi hain jo maange the.
real_world_analogy: Library mein book ko uske title se nahi, uske har page ke fingerprint se dhundhna: fingerprint match hua toh book wahi hai, chahe kisi bhi shelf (CDN) se aayi ho.
how_it_works: SHA-256 collision-resistant hai: do alag byte strings ka same hash practically nahi milta. Isliye digest ek unique, self-verifying naam ban jaata hai.
in_this_project: image.py: sha256_bytes, sha256_file (gzip.open ya open, CHUNK = 1 << 20), check_digest, DigestMismatch exception. registry.py ka _verify_blob aur Registry.manifest dono check_digest call karte hain.
advantages: Verification ke liye kisi server par trust nahi
Same naam = same bytes, caching aasaan
Ek hi chhota function, sab jagah reuse
disadvantages: Sirf sha256 support (sha512 digests reject)
Hash nikalne ke liye poora blob padhna padta hai
common_mistakes: Expected digest ka format check na karna
Manifest ko parse karke dobara serialize karke hash karna (bytes badal jaate hain)
Compressed aur uncompressed hash mix kar dena
follow_up_questions: Manifest ka hash parse kiye hue JSON par kyun nahi, raw bytes par kyun?
sha512 digest support karna ho toh check_digest mein kya badlega?

question: How does an image layer record that a file was deleted? Explain '.wh.name' and '.wh..wh..opq' whiteouts.
answer_hinglish:
Layer ek tar hai jisme sirf woh files hain jo is layer ne add ya change ki. Lekin delete kaise batayein? Tar mein 'yeh file nahi hai' likhne ka koi type nahi, toh OCI ne naming convention banayi: WHITEOUT files.

- dir/.wh.name: matlab lower layers mein jo 'dir/name' tha, woh is layer mein delete hai. Agar name ek directory tha, toh poori directory recursively jaati hai (test_whiteout_deletes_lower_directory_recursively: '.wh.var' poora var/ hata deta hai).
- dir/.wh..wh..opq: OPAQUE marker. Matlab 'dir' ke andar jo kuch LOWER layers ne rakha tha woh sab hide, lekin is layer ki apni files dir mein rehti hain.

minibox/image.py mein classify(rel) path ko dekhta hai: base == WH_OPAQUE toh Whiteout('opaque', parent); base '.wh.' se shuru toh Whiteout('file', parent/name); warna None (normal entry). Bad names reject: 'etc/.wh.' (khaali naam) aur 'etc/.wh...' (naam '..') -> UnsafePath, kyunki '.wh...' ka target parent directory ban jaata. Aur 'etc/x.wh.y' whiteout NAHI hai -- prefix sirf basename ki shuruaat mein maana jaata hai (test_classify).

Whiteout file khud rootfs mein kabhi nahi likhi jaati: test_whiteout_deletes_lower_file check karta hai ki 'etc/.wh.motd' tree mein nahi hai aur etc/motd gayab hai. Mutations M23 (whiteouts plain files ki tarah extract, 5 tests red) aur M24 (opaque ignore, 3 red) isko cover karte hain.
why_needed: Layered images mein upper layer ko neeche ki file hatani hoti hai (jaise apk cache saaf karna) bina lower layer ko badle.
real_world_analogy: Purane register mein entry kaatne ki jagah ek nayi line likhna 'entry no. 12 cancelled' -- register (lower layer) waisa hi hai, lekin final hisaab mein woh entry nahi gini jaati.
how_it_works: Apply karte waqt har member ka naam classify hota hai; whiteout mila toh target ko rootfs se delete karo (file: ek entry, opaque: directory ke saare children), aur whiteout entry ko extract mat karo.
in_this_project: image.py: WH_PREFIX = '.wh.', WH_OPAQUE = '.wh..wh..opq', Whiteout dataclass (kind, target), classify, apply_whiteout, _remove (symlink ya file -> unlink, directory -> rmtree).
advantages: Plain tar format mein deletion express ho jaata hai
Lower layers immutable rehte hain
disadvantages: Naming convention hai, koi alag type nahi -- '.wh.' se shuru hone wali asli file image mein nahi rakh sakte
Overlayfs ka apna whiteout format alag hai, convert karna padta hai
common_mistakes: Whiteout file ko rootfs mein extract kar dena
Opaque ko 'directory delete' samajhna (directory rehti hai, sirf lower children jaate hain)
'.wh...' jaise naam ko validate na karna
follow_up_questions: Ek layer mein whiteout aur same naam ki nayi file dono ho toh kya bachta hai?
Overlayfs container ke andar delete ko kaise record karta hai, aur woh layer ke .wh. se kaise alag hai?

question: What are overlayfs's lowerdir, upperdir, workdir and merged, and how does minibox use them so the image is never modified?
answer_hinglish:
Overlayfs ek union filesystem hai: do directories ko upar-neeche rakh kar ek combined view dikhata hai.

- lowerdir: read-only base. minibox mein yeh image ka flattened rootfs hai (jo pull ne banaya).
- upperdir: writable layer. Container jo bhi likhta, badalta ya delete karta hai, sab yahan jaata hai. File modify hui toh pehle copy-up hoti hai (lower se upper mein copy), phir change.
- workdir: overlayfs ka scratch dir (atomic copy-up waghera ke liye), upper ke SAME filesystem par hona chahiye.
- merged: mount point jahan combined view dikhta hai; yahi container ka / banta hai (pivot_root ke baad).

minibox/container.py ka run() har container ke liye <state-dir>/<name>/ banata hai (default /run/minibox, mode 0700, aur makedirs fail ho jaata hai agar naam already use mein hai), uske andar upper, work, merged. mounts.OverlayDirs yeh char paths rakhta hai, overlay_options string banata hai 'lowerdir=..,upperdir=..,workdir=..', aur build_plan step 2 mein Mount('overlay', merged, 'overlay', 0, options) daalta hai. Container exit ke baad cleanup() poora state dir rmtree karta hai -- upper delete matlab saare changes gaye.

Proof: test_writes_do_not_reach_the_image_and_vanish (/root/new-file image mein nahi, /etc/motd wapas aata hai agle container mein) aur test_image_rootfs_is_unchanged_after_many_runs ('rm -rf /usr/share', 'chmod 777 /bin' ke baad bhi image ka snapshot same). Mutation M19 (overlay ki jagah image ka bind mount) ne 5 mein se 4 overlay tests red kiye.
why_needed: Ek image se kai containers chalane hain, har ek apne writes ke saath, bina image copy kiye aur bina image kharab kiye.
real_world_analogy: Ek printed map par transparent sheet rakh kar marker se likhna: map (lower) saaf rehta hai, sheet (upper) phenk do toh sab changes gaye, aur doosre bande ko apni alag sheet milti hai.
how_it_works: Read: pehle upper mein dhundho, nahi mila toh lower. Write: upper mein (copy-up agar file lower mein thi). Delete: upper mein ek whiteout (0/0 char device) taaki lower ki file chhup jaaye.
in_this_project: container.py run() dirs banata hai; mounts.py OverlayDirs (lower, upper, work, merged ke comments ke saath), overlay_options, build_plan; container.py cleanup() rmtree(state). Tests: tests/integration/test_overlay.py.
code_example:
# real, minibox/mounts.py
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OverlayDirs:
    lower: str     # the image rootfs, never written
    upper: str     # this container's changes
    work: str      # overlayfs scratch dir, same filesystem as upper
    merged: str    # where the combined view is mounted; becomes the container's /
advantages: Image copy nahi hoti, container start sasta (18 ms inner median measured)
Har container isolated writes
Cleanup = ek directory delete
disadvantages: Pehli baar badi file modify karne par copy-up cost
workdir aur upper same filesystem par hone chahiye
common_mistakes: workdir ko alag filesystem par rakhna
Sochna ki lowerdir mein writes jaate hain
merged ko hi upperdir samajhna

--no-overlay mode mein kya badalta hai?
Copy-up kya hai aur kab hota hai?

question: Walk through parse_reference: how does 'alpine:3.20' become registry-1.docker.io / library/alpine / 3.20, and how are other registries and digest references detected?
answer_hinglish:
parse_reference(text) ek Reference(registry, repository, tag, digest) dataclass return karta hai. Rules order mein:

1) '@' hai toh peeche ka hissa digest; regex sha256:[0-9a-f]{64} se fullmatch hona chahiye, warna ValueError ('alpine@sha256:xyz' reject).
2) Pehla '/' tak ka part (first) REGISTRY tabhi maana jaata hai jab '/' ho AUR first mein '.' ya ':' ho ya first == 'localhost'. Isliye 'ghcr.io/owner/repo' -> ghcr.io, 'localhost:5000/x' -> localhost:5000, lekin 'someuser/app' -> Docker Hub par someuser/app. Yeh Docker ka hi heuristic hai.
3) Tag: sirf AAKHRI path component mein ':' dekha jaata hai (rsplit('/')[-1]) -- isliye 'localhost:5000/x' mein port ko tag nahi samjha jaata.
4) Docker Hub par repository mein '/' nahi hai toh 'library/' prefix lagta hai: official images library/ namespace mein rehti hain. alpine -> library/alpine.
5) Repo name regex (lowercase, ., _, - separators) aur tag regex ([A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}) validate hote hain: 'Alpine', 'a/../b', 'alpine:bad tag', '' sab ValueError.
6) Na tag na digest -> tag = 'latest'.

Reference.ref property digest ko tag par prefer karti hai: 'alpine@sha256:...' mein manifest seedha digest se fetch hoga, aur tab manifest() hash ko us digest se compare karega. Tests: test_parse_reference (7 cases) aur test_parse_reference_rejects (5 cases).
why_needed: User 'alpine' likhta hai lekin HTTP request ko host, repo path aur ref chahiye; galat parse = galat image ya galat host ko token request.
real_world_analogy: Postal address ko parse karna: agar pehle hisse mein PIN code ya city jaisa kuch (dot/colon) hai toh woh sheher hai, warna default sheher (Docker Hub) maan lo.
how_it_works: String split: '@' -> digest, pehla '/' -> registry heuristic, aakhri component ka ':' -> tag, phir defaults aur regex validation.
in_this_project: registry.py: Reference dataclass with ref property, parse_reference, DOCKER_HUB = 'registry-1.docker.io'. Registry.__init__ base URL banata hai: https://<registry>/v2/<repository>.
advantages: Docker CLI jaisa hi behaviour, user ko surprise nahi
Galat input jaldi ValueError se ruk jaata hai
Digest ref end-to-end verification enable karta hai
disadvantages: Heuristic hai: dot ke bina koi private registry hostname ('myregistry/x') Docker Hub samjha jaayega
Sirf sha256 digests
common_mistakes: Port wale registry mein ':' ko tag samajh lena
library/ prefix bhool jaana (Docker Hub 401/404 deta hai)
Repo names mein uppercase allow karna
follow_up_questions: 'myhost/app:1' kis registry par jaayega aur kyun?
Tag aur digest dono diye ho ('alpine:3.20@sha256:...') toh yeh code kya karta hai?

question: How does minibox get an anonymous bearer token from Docker Hub? Explain the 401 challenge, parse_www_authenticate and the retry in Registry.get.
answer_hinglish:
Docker Hub public images ke liye bhi token maangta hai, lekin anonymous token free milta hai. Flow:

1) Registry.get pehli GET bina Authorization ke bhejta hai. Response 401 aata hai header ke saath: WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="https://auth.docker.io/token",service="registry.docker.io",scope="repository:library/alpine:pull".
2) get() check karta hai: status 401, 'www-authenticate' header hai, aur self.token abhi None hai -> _authenticate(challenge).
3) parse_www_authenticate scheme ko space par alag karta hai; 'bearer' (case-insensitive) nahi hai toh RegistryError (Basic support nahi). Phir regex (\w+)="([^"]*)" se key=value pairs ki dict. realm nahi hai toh RegistryError.
4) _authenticate sirf service aur scope query mein rakhta hai, scope missing ho toh default repository:<repo>:pull, URL = realm + '?' + urlencode(query), fetch karta hai (bina headers), body JSON se 'token' ya 'access_token' leta hai. Token na mile ya status 200 na ho -> RegistryError.
5) Same request dobara, ab _headers() 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' jodta hai. Token object par store hai, isliye baaki saare manifests aur blobs isi se jaate hain.

FakeRegistry yahi Docker Hub behaviour imitate karta hai aur test_pull_end_to_end_with_token_index_and_whiteouts assert karta hai ki auth URL sirf EK baar call hua. FakeRegistry token URL mein 'scope=repository%3Alibrary%2Falpine%3Apull' bhi assert karta hai, yaani scope sahi encode hua. Limitation: token ek hi baar liya jaata hai (self.token is None condition), expire hone par refresh nahi hota -- doosra 401 seedha 'HTTP 401' error ban jaata hai.
why_needed: Registry ko pata hona chahiye ki kis repo par kaunsa access (pull) diya, chahe user anonymous ho; isliye token per-scope milta hai.
real_world_analogy: Museum ki gate par guard bolta hai 'ticket counter wahan hai' (realm). Aap free ticket (anonymous token) lekar aate ho aur phir har gallery mein wahi ticket dikhate ho.
how_it_works: HTTP 401 + WWW-Authenticate challenge -> token server (realm) se service+scope ke liye token -> original request Authorization: Bearer ke saath retry.
in_this_project: registry.py: parse_www_authenticate, Registry._authenticate, Registry.get, Registry._headers. Unit test test_parse_www_authenticate Basic aur realm-less challenges ko reject karte dekhta hai.
advantages: Hardcoded auth URL nahi, challenge se discover hota hai -- doosri registries bhi chal sakti hain
Token ek baar, baaki requests reuse
Retry sirf ek baar, infinite loop nahi
disadvantages: Token expiry/refresh handle nahi
Credentials (private images) support nahi
Regex parser escaped quotes handle nahi karta
common_mistakes: realm ko hardcode kar dena
Har request par naya token lena
401 par bina limit ke retry loop

Bada layer download karte waqt token expire ho jaaye toh kya hoga?

question: How does select_platform pick a manifest from an image index, and why does arm64 need special handling for the 'v8' variant?
answer_hinglish:
Index mein 'manifests' list hoti hai, har entry ke paas platform {os, architecture, variant?}. select_platform(index, os_name, arch, variant) har entry check karta hai:

- os ya architecture match nahi -> skip.
- 'if variant and p.get("variant") and p.get("variant") != variant' -> skip. Matlab variant tabhi filter karta hai jab DONO taraf diya ho. arm64 kabhi 'variant: v8' ke saath publish hota hai, kabhi bina variant ke; isliye hum v8 maangein aur index mein variant na ho, tab bhi match hona chahiye.
- Bache hue candidates mein se PEHLA return.
- Koi candidate nahi -> RegistryError('no manifest for linux/riscv64 in index (have: linux/amd64, linux/arm, ...)') -- error mein available platforms list hote hain, debugging aasaan.

Platform kahan se aata hai: host_platform() platform.machine() map karta hai: x86_64/amd64 -> amd64, aarch64/arm64 -> arm64, aur arm64 ke liye variant 'v8', warna None. CLI '--platform os/arch[/variant]' se override de sakta hai (cli.parse_args 2 ya 3 parts validate karta hai). Server Ampere A1 (aarch64) tha, toh alpine:3.20 ka linux/arm64 manifest chuna gaya.

test_select_platform: arm64+v8 -> entry 3; arm64 + None variant -> bhi entry 3; amd64 -> entry 1; riscv64 -> error with 'linux/riscv64'; arm v6 -> error (index mein sirf arm v7 hai). Ek 'unknown/unknown' entry bhi index mein hai -- Docker Hub attestation manifests aise hi dikhte hain, aur yeh code unhe os match na hone se skip kar deta hai.
why_needed: Multi-arch tag ek hi naam se kai binaries deta hai; galat arch ka rootfs chalaoge toh exec 'exec format error' dega.
real_world_analogy: Kapde ki dukaan mein ek design (tag) kai sizes (platforms) mein: aap apna size maangte ho; 'M' size par 'slim fit' label ho ya na ho, M toh M hai.
how_it_works: Linear filter: os+arch exact, variant sirf tab jab dono side present; first match return; khaali par descriptive error.
in_this_project: registry.py: host_platform, select_platform; pull() mein platform_ or host_platform(). cli.py --platform. Test INDEX constant mein amd64, arm v7, arm64 v8, unknown entries.
advantages: Missing variant ko tolerate karta hai (real-world arm64 indexes)
Clear error message with available platforms
Platform override CLI se testing ke liye
disadvantages: Pehla candidate -- agar ek platform ke do entries hon toh koi preference nahi
os.version / features fields ignore
common_mistakes: Variant ko strict match karna (arm64 bina variant wala index fail)
uname machine ('aarch64') ko seedha OCI architecture maan lena
Attestation entries ('unknown/unknown') ko image samajh lena

question: Why does an image have both a layer digest and a diff_id? What exactly does each one hash, and how does minibox check both?
answer_hinglish:
Ek hi layer ke do hashes hote hain kyunki do alag cheezein verify karni hain:

- Layer DIGEST (manifest ke layers[i].digest): COMPRESSED blob (tar+gzip) ke bytes ka sha256. Yeh transport/storage ka naam hai -- registry isi naam se blob serve karta hai.
- diff_id (config ke rootfs.diff_ids[i]): UNCOMPRESSED tar stream ka sha256. Yeh content ka naam hai, compression se independent. Same tar ko alag gzip level se compress karo toh digest badlega, diff_id nahi.

Dono kyun? Digest prove karta hai 'jo download hua woh wahi blob hai jo manifest ne kaha'. diff_id prove karta hai 'is blob ka content wahi hai jo CONFIG kehta hai', aur config khud digest se manifest se juda hai. Toh chain banti hai: manifest -> config -> diff_ids -> layer content.

minibox mein pull() har layer par: _verify_blob(p, layer['digest'], 'layer i') (compressed), size match, phir _verify_blob(p, diff_id, 'layer i diff_id', gunzip=lt in GZIP_LAYER_TYPES) -- image.sha256_file gunzip=True ke saath gzip.open se stream karke decompressed bytes hash karta hai. Plain tar layer ke liye dono same hash hote hain. Pehle yeh bhi check: len(diff_ids) == len(layers), warna RegistryError.

test_diff_id_is_digest_of_uncompressed_tar dono hashes ka farak dikhata hai. test_diff_id_mismatch_is_refused mazedaar hai: config mein diff_ids ka ORDER reverse kar diya, manifest aur index sahi digests ke saath dobara banaye -- har blob apne digest se match karta hai, phir bhi pull DigestMismatch('diff_id') deta hai. Mutation M21 (diff_id check hata do) isi test se pakda gaya.
why_needed: Sirf compressed digest se pata nahi chalta ki layer ka content config se consistent hai, aur layer order ki galti pakad mein nahi aati.
real_world_analogy: Parcel par courier ka barcode (digest) batata hai sahi parcel aaya; andar ki packing list (diff_id) batati hai ki dibbe ke andar wahi saaman hai jo order mein tha.
how_it_works: digest = sha256(gzip bytes); diff_id = sha256(gunzip(gzip bytes)). Pull dono compute karta hai, ek ek baar file padh kar.
in_this_project: registry.py pull() layer loop; image.py sha256_file(path, gunzip); tests: test_image.py::test_diff_id_is_digest_of_uncompressed_tar, test_registry.py::test_diff_id_mismatch_is_refused.
code_example:
# real, minibox/registry.py pull layer loop (trimmed)
p = reg.blob(layer["digest"], blobs)
size = os.path.getsize(p)
_verify_blob(p, layer["digest"], f"layer {i}")
if "size" in layer and layer["size"] != size:
    raise image.DigestMismatch(f"layer {i}: size {size} != manifest size {layer['size']}")
_verify_blob(p, diff_id, f"layer {i} diff_id", gunzip=lt in GZIP_LAYER_TYPES)
advantages: Compression badalne par bhi content identity stable
Layer order ki galti pakdi jaati hai
Transport aur content dono verify
disadvantages: Har layer do baar padhni padti hai (ek compressed, ek decompress karke)
gzip decompress CPU cost
common_mistakes: diff_id ko compressed blob par compute karna
Layers aur diff_ids ki ginti compare na karna
Sirf digest check karke sochna ki content bhi verified hai
follow_up_questions: Dono hashes ek hi read pass mein kaise nikaloge?
zstd layers aaye toh diff_id kaise compute hoga?

question: How does Registry.manifest verify a manifest? Why is a manifest fetched by digest checked differently from one fetched by tag (Docker-Content-Digest)?
answer_hinglish:
Registry.manifest(ref) manifest GET karta hai (Accept mein saare INDEX_TYPES + MANIFEST_TYPES), size limit lagata hai (MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES = 4 MiB; urllib_fetch MAX+1 bytes padhta hai taaki 'too large' detect ho sake), aur EXACT raw bytes ka sha256 nikalta hai. Phir do raste:

1) ref 'sha256:' se shuru hai (BY DIGEST): image.check_digest(digest, ref, 'manifest'). Yeh poora content addressing hai -- humne naam maanga, bytes ka hash naam se match hona chahiye. Index se chuna gaya platform manifest hamesha isi raaste se aata hai, aur 'alpine@sha256:...' wala user ref bhi.
2) TAG se ('3.20'): tag ek mutable naam hai, iske against koi independent hash nahi hai. Toh agar registry ne Docker-Content-Digest header bheja hai, uske against check karte hain. Yeh tampering nahi rokta (jo registry header bhejti hai wahi body bhejti hai), lekin corrupted ya truncated body pakad leta hai.

Return (doc, media, digest): media pehle JSON ke mediaType se, warna Content-Type header se (';' ke pehle ka hissa). Raw bytes par hash zaroori hai: FakeRegistry ka tamper='manifest' sirf whitespace badalta hai ('"schemaVersion": 2' -> do spaces) -- JSON semantically same, lekin bytes alag, toh digest mismatch aur pull refuse. Agar hum json.loads + json.dumps karke hash karte toh yeh pakda nahi jaata aur asli manifests (jo kisi aur formatting mein serialized hain) bhi kabhi match nahi karte.

Honest gap: tag fetch par header na ho toh koi check nahi hota (elif branch). FakeRegistry content-digest header nahi bhejta, isliye tag wala index unit tests mein unchecked hai; uske andar ke digests baad mein verify hote hain.
why_needed: Manifest poori image ki root hai; ise verify kiye bina neeche ke saare digests bhi bharose ke laayak nahi.
real_world_analogy: Bank cheque: agar cheque number (digest) se maanga toh number match hona chahiye. Agar sirf 'mera latest cheque' (tag) maanga, toh bank jo slip saath deta hai usi se check kar sakte ho ki cheque phata hua toh nahi -- lekin bank par trust karna padta hai.
how_it_works: Hash over raw bytes; by-digest -> ref se compare; by-tag -> Docker-Content-Digest se compare agar present; phir JSON parse.
in_this_project: registry.py Registry.manifest, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES, ACCEPT; tests: test_tampered_content_is_refused_and_nothing_is_applied[manifest].
code_example:
# real, minibox/registry.py Registry.manifest (trimmed)
digest = image.sha256_bytes(r.body)
if ref.startswith("sha256:"):
    image.check_digest(digest, ref, "manifest")   # content addressed: the bytes ARE the name
elif "docker-content-digest" in r.headers:
    image.check_digest(digest, r.headers["docker-content-digest"], "manifest (Docker-Content-Digest)")
doc = json.loads(r.body)
advantages: Raw bytes hash -> serialization differences se bachav
Size limit se badi/malicious manifest memory nahi khaati
Tag path par bhi corruption check
disadvantages: Tag path par header absent ho toh koi check nahi
Tag path par trust registry/TLS par hi hai
common_mistakes: Parsed-and-reserialized JSON ka hash lena
Docker-Content-Digest ko tampering protection samajhna
Manifest size limit na lagana
follow_up_questions: Header absent ho toh kya karna chahiye -- warn, fail ya ignore?
Tag ka trust badhane ke liye signatures (cosign/notation) kaise fit hote?

question: Blob downloads redirect to a CDN. How does minibox make sure the registry bearer token is never sent to the CDN, and how is that unit tested?
answer_hinglish:
Docker Hub blob GET par usually 307 redirect deta hai kisi CDN URL par. Python ka urllib redirect follow karte waqt original request ke NORMAL headers naye request par copy kar deta hai. Agar Authorization normal header hota, toh hamara registry token ek third-party host ko chala jaata -- token leak.

Fix urllib_fetch mein ek line ka hai: header ka naam 'authorization' (case-insensitive) hai toh req.add_unredirected_header(k, v), baaki headers req.add_header. urllib ka HTTPRedirectHandler.redirect_request naye Request mein sirf normal headers le jaata hai, unredirected nahi. Toh registry ko token jaata hai, CDN ko nahi. CDN URL waise bhi khud signed hota hai, use token ki zaroorat nahi.

Do unit tests:
1) test_authorization_header_is_not_forwarded_on_redirect: urllib ka contract khud check karta hai -- ek Request par unredirected Authorization aur normal Accept, redirect_request(... 307 ..., 'https://cdn.example/blob') ke baad naye request mein Authorization None.
2) test_urllib_fetch_marks_the_token_unredirected: HAMARA urllib_fetch drive karta hai. monkeypatch se urllib.request.urlopen ko fake se badla; fake jo Request milta hai use real HTTPRedirectHandler se redirect karwata hai aur record karta hai: original Authorization 'Bearer secret', redirected None, aur Accept dono mein present. Yeh doosra test isliye zaroori hai ki pehla sirf library ka behaviour prove karta tha, hamara code nahi.

Mutation M29 (token redirects par bhi bhejo, yaani add_header) ne 1 test red kiya. Yeh wahi bug class hai jo curl/requests mein bhi CVEs ban chuki hai.
why_needed: Bearer token se registry par access milta hai; CDN ek alag party hai, use token dena least-privilege ke against hai aur log/cache mein leak ho sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Building ke reception par aap apna ID card dikhate ho; reception aapko courier office bhejta hai. Courier ko ID card ki photocopy dene ki zaroorat nahi -- unke paas apna slip hai.
how_it_works: urllib.request.Request do header dicts rakhta hai: headers (redirect par copy) aur unredirected_hdrs (sirf is request ke liye). redirect_request naya Request banata hai sirf pehle wale se.
in_this_project: registry.py urllib_fetch (comment ke saath), tests test_registry.py ke do redirect tests. Integration run mein real Docker Hub pull (alpine:3.20) isi code se hua.
advantages: Ek line ka fix, stdlib feature
Test hamare function ko real redirect logic se guzaarta hai
Accept jaise harmless headers redirect par bhi jaate hain
disadvantages: urllib ke internal behaviour par depend
Agar koi custom opener/handler jode toh dobara verify karna padega
common_mistakes: Sirf library behaviour test karna, apna code nahi
Har header unredirected bana dena (Accept bhi khona)
Redirect same-host hai ya nahi bina dekhe token bhejna

requests library mein yeh default kaise handle hota hai?
Token ko logs mein aane se kaise rokoge?

question: The HTTP layer of the puller is injectable ('fetch'). How does that make the whole pull testable without a network, and what does FakeRegistry simulate?
answer_hinglish:
registry.py mein Fetch ek type alias hai: Callable[[str, dict[str, str], str | None], Fetched] -- fetch(url, headers, save_to) -> Fetched(status, headers lowercase, body). Real implementation urllib_fetch hai (save_to diya toh body file mein stream). Registry(ref, fetch=urllib_fetch) aur pull(reference, dest, fetch=urllib_fetch, ...) dono isko parameter ki tarah lete hain. Bas yahi seam hai: tests apna callable de dete hain.

tests/unit/test_registry.py ka FakeRegistry ek callable class hai jo Docker Hub jaisa behave karta hai:
- Authorization 'Bearer T0K' nahi hai toh 401 + asli jaisa WWW-Authenticate challenge.
- auth.docker.io/token URL par token JSON, aur assert ki scope sahi URL-encoded hai.
- manifests/<ref>: '3.20' tag par index (amd64 dummy + arm64 v8 asli manifest) ya use_index=False par seedha manifest; digest par manifest; nahi mila toh 404.
- blobs/<digest>: save_to file mein likh deta hai.
- self.calls har request record karta hai (isse 'token ek hi baar mila' assert hota hai).
- tamper='layer' | 'config' | 'manifest' ek byte/field badal deta hai taaki verification fail ho.
Layers tests/unit/layers.py ka make_tar memory mein banata hai (PAX format, fixed mtime, gzip mtime=0, toh deterministic).

Is se 140 unit tests Windows par bhi chalte hain (5 skip: symlinks, POSIX modes). Real Docker Hub sirf ek integration test mein (test_pull_alpine_from_docker_hub, @pytest.mark.network). Mutations M20-M29 sab isi unit suite se pakde gaye -- network ke bina.
why_needed: Network tests slow, flaky aur hostile cases (tampered blobs) reproduce nahi kar sakte; fake se har failure mode deterministic test hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Flight simulator: pilot asli plane ke bina engine failure, storm sab practice karta hai; asli flight (Docker Hub test) kabhi kabhi.
how_it_works: Dependency injection via a plain function parameter: production default urllib_fetch, test mein ek object jiska __call__ same signature follow karta hai.
in_this_project: registry.py Fetched dataclass, Fetch alias, Registry.__init__(fetch=...), pull(fetch=...). test_registry.py FakeRegistry, two_layers(), ARM constant. layers.py make_tar, digest.

Tampering jaise hostile cases aasaani se
No mocking library -- ek simple callable
disadvantages: Fake asli registry se drift kar sakta hai (jaise Docker-Content-Digest header nahi bhejta)
Redirects fake mein nahi -- unke liye alag tests

Fake ko itna simple banana ki 401 flow test hi na ho
Sirf happy path test karna

Redirect aur slow responses ko fake mein kaise simulate karoge?

question: Describe the on-disk layout of a pulled image (blobs/sha256/<hex>, manifest.json, config.json, rootfs). How are blobs written, and why is a failed blob deleted?
answer_hinglish:
minibox ke paas database nahi hai, lekin pull ka output ek chhota content-addressed store hai -- ise ek key-value table ki tarah design kiya gaya hai jahan KEY = digest aur VALUE = bytes:

<dest>/blobs/sha256/<64 hex>  -- config aur har layer blob, file ka naam hi uska digest
<dest>/manifest.json          -- chuna gaya platform manifest
<dest>/config.json            -- config blob ki copy
<dest>/rootfs/                -- flattened layers, overlay ka lowerdir

Write path (Registry.blob): path = blobs/<hex>. Agar file pehle se hai toh download skip. Warna pehle <hex>.part mein download (save_to se stream), phir os.replace(tmp, path) -- atomic rename, toh half-written file kabhi final naam par nahi dikhti.

Key ka invariant 'file ka content uske naam ka hash hai' hona chahiye. Isliye _verify_blob fail hone par os.unlink(path) karta hai: agar bad blob rakha rehta, toh agle pull par blob() use 'already exists' maan kar skip kar deta -- corrupted entry hamesha ke liye cache ban jaati. Verification hamesha chalti hai, cached file par bhi, toh yeh double safety hai. Test test_failed_blob_is_deleted_not_cached: tampered layer ke baad blobs/ directory mein uska hex nahi hona chahiye.

rootfs har pull par shutil.rmtree karke naya banta hai (incremental update nahi). Limitations (README NOT-done): images ke beech koi shared cache nahi (har pull apne dest mein complete), koi gc/refcount nahi, aur ek .part file crash ke baad pada reh sakta hai (blob() use reuse nahi karta, overwrite karega).
why_needed: Content-addressed layout deduplication, resume aur integrity checking ko natural bana deta hai -- naam se hi pata hai content kya hona chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Godown jahan har dibbe par uske andar ke saaman ka fingerprint label hai: dibba khol kar fingerprint match nahi hua toh dibba phenk do, label ke saath shelf par mat rakho.
how_it_works: Key = sha256 digest, value = file; write = temp file + atomic rename; read = verify hash; failed verify = delete.
in_this_project: registry.py Registry.blob (.part + os.replace), _verify_blob (unlink on DigestMismatch), pull() (blobs dir, rootfs rmtree, manifest.json, config.json copy).
advantages: Naam hi integrity check hai
Atomic rename se half files final naam par nahi
Same layout OCI image-layout jaisa
disadvantages: Shared cache nahi, har image apna copy
GC/refcount nahi
Har pull par rootfs poora dobara
common_mistakes: Download seedha final naam par likhna
Failed blob ko cache mein chhod dena
Cached file ko bina verify reuse karna
follow_up_questions: Kai images ke beech ek blob store share karna ho toh GC kaise karoge?
Do parallel pulls same blob download karein toh race kaise handle hoga?

question: Why does apply_layer process each layer in two passes (whiteouts first, then regular entries)? What would break with a single pass?
answer_hinglish:
OCI spec kehta hai: whiteout sirf LOWER layers ka content chhupata hai, us layer ki apni files ko kabhi nahi. Lekin tar ke andar entries ka order kuch bhi ho sakta hai -- whiteout pehle aa sakta hai ya baad mein.

Agar single pass mein tar order follow karo: layer mein 'var/cache/new' pehle aur 'var/cache/.wh..wh..opq' baad mein hai, toh opaque marker aate hi var/cache ke saare children delete -- including 'new' jo ISI layer ne abhi likhi thi. Ya 'etc/motd' (nayi) phir 'etc/.wh.motd' -- nayi motd bhi delete. Galat result.

apply_layer isliye do loops chalata hai:
Pass 1: tf.getmembers() par loop, har naam clean_member_path se saaf, classify se whiteout hai toh apply_whiteout(root, wh) turant (abhi rootfs mein sirf lower layers ka content hai), counts update. Normal entries 'regular' list mein jama.
Pass 2: regular entries extract.
Is order mein whiteouts kabhi is layer ki files ko dekh hi nahi paate.

Tests: test_opaque_dir_hides_lower_children_but_keeps_this_layers_files (opaque marker tar mein 'new' ke BAAD hai, phir bhi new = '3' bachta hai, a aur b gaye), test_whiteout_does_not_hide_a_file_of_the_same_layer (re-added motd = 'new'), test_whiteout_of_missing_file_is_harmless. Mutation M25 ('whiteouts applied after the layer's own files') ne 4 tests red kiye. Pass 2 mein ek aur detail: agar layer file ko directory se badal rahi hai ya ulta, toh purana entry pehle _remove hota hai (tarfile yeh khud nahi karta) -- test_upper_layer_replaces_file_with_directory_and_back.
why_needed: Spec ka semantics tar order par depend nahi karna chahiye; warna same layer alag tools se alag rootfs banayegi.
real_world_analogy: Ghar renovate karna: pehle purana furniture hatao (whiteouts), phir naya rakho. Agar naya sofa rakhne ke baad 'drawing room khaali karo' order follow kiya, toh naya sofa bhi chala jaayega.
how_it_works: getmembers() ek baar padhta hai; whiteouts turant apply, regular entries buffer, phir buffer extract.
in_this_project: image.py apply_layer (do loops), apply_whiteout, _remove; tests test_image.py ke whiteout tests aur test_registry.py two_layers() (layer 1 mein .wh.motd + opaque var).

# real, minibox/image.py apply_layer (trimmed)
for m in members:
    rel = clean_member_path(m.name)
    wh = classify(rel)
    if wh is None:
        if rel:
            regular.append((rel, m))
        continue
    apply_whiteout(root, wh)
    counts["whiteouts" if wh.kind == "file" else "opaque"] += 1
for rel, m in regular:
    path = _inside(root, rel)
    ...
    tf.extract(m, root, numeric_owner=True, filter=_keep_mode)
advantages: Tar order se independent, spec-correct
Simple implementation, sirf ek list buffer
disadvantages: getmembers() saare TarInfo memory mein rakhta hai (gzip stream do baar random access ke liye seekable chahiye)
Bahut bade layers ke liye memory
common_mistakes: Tar order mein hi whiteouts apply karna
Opaque marker ko poori directory delete samajhna
File<->directory replacement handle na karna

Overlayfs per-layer lowerdirs use karte toh whiteouts kab aur kaise convert hote?

question: How does clean_member_path protect against '..' path traversal in layer tars, and why does the README call it 'two lines of defense'?
answer_hinglish:
Layer tar untrusted input hai -- registry se aaya hai. Agar member naam '../evil' ya 'etc/../../x' ho aur hum seedha root/naam par likh dein, toh file rootfs ke BAHAR (host par) chali jaayegi. Classic 'zip slip'.

clean_member_path(name) har member par sabse pehle chalta hai (whiteouts par bhi):
- backslash ko '/' banata hai,
- leading './' aur '/' hata deta hai (layer tars dono style use karte hain; '/etc/passwd' -> 'etc/passwd', yaani absolute naam bhi rootfs ke andar hi jaata hai),
- '/' par split, khaali aur '.' parts hata deta hai ('etc//x/./y' -> 'etc/x/y'),
- koi bhi part '..' hai toh UnsafePath. Note: yeh normalise karke '..' ko 'cancel' nahi karta -- 'a/..' bhi reject hai. Simple rule: '..' kahin bhi = refuse.
- './' -> '' (root khud), jise apply_layer skip karta hai.

Hard links ke liye bhi m.linkname = clean_member_path(m.linkname), taaki hardlink target bahar na ho. Tests: test_clean_member_path_rejects_dotdot (4 cases), test_dotdot_member_is_refused (tmp_path/evil nahi bana), test_dotdot_whiteout_is_refused ('../.wh.victim' se bahar ki victim file delete nahi hui -- whiteouts bhi delete operation hain, unhe bhi bachana zaroori).

'Two lines of defense': mutation M26 ('..' check hata do) sirf name-check unit test se pakda gaya (4 red). Apply ke waqt Python ka tarfile.tar_filter (jo _keep_mode mein chalta hai) bhi '../x' ko refuse kar deta, toh regular files ke liye do layers hain. Lekin whiteouts tarfile ke paas jaate hi nahi -- woh hamara apna delete code hai -- toh wahan clean_member_path hi akela guard hai.
why_needed: Untrusted archive extraction ka sabse common bug path traversal hai; root ke roop mein chalne wala puller host ki koi bhi file overwrite/delete kar sakta.
real_world_analogy: Courier ko bola 'yeh parcel ghar ke andar rakh do', aur parcel par likha hai '../padosi ka ghar'. Guard ka rule: address mein '..' dikhe toh parcel wapas.
how_it_works: Normalise -> reject '..' -> relative path return. Phir _inside() symlinks ke through escape check karta hai, aur tarfile filter apni checks karta hai.
in_this_project: image.py clean_member_path, UnsafePath; apply_layer har member aur hardlink linkname par call karta hai.
advantages: Simple, strict rule -- edge cases kam
Whiteouts aur hardlinks dono cover
Absolute names bhi rootfs ke andar map
disadvantages: 'a/b/../c' jaise legit (lekin rare) names bhi reject
Symlink escape yeh function nahi pakadta -- uske liye _inside
common_mistakes: '..' ko normpath se resolve karke allow karna
Whiteout paths ko validate na karna
Hardlink linkname bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: Symlink ke through escape clean_member_path kyun nahi pakad sakta?
Python 3.12 ka tarfile filter='data' kya alag karta hai?

question: Where is the overlay mounted, why does that make cleanup simple, and how is a deletion inside the container different from a '.wh.' file in a layer?
answer_hinglish:
Overlay mount mounts.build_plan ka step 2 hai, aur plan INIT (container ka PID 1) apne NAYE mount namespace mein apply karta hai, pehle step 1 'mount(NULL, /, MS_REC|MS_PRIVATE)' ke baad. Matlab overlay mount sirf container ke namespace mein exist karta hai, host ke /proc/mounts mein kabhi nahi dikhta (mutation M4 ne dikhaya ki private na karo toh 10 mounts host mein leak hue).

Cleanup simple kyun: jab CMD exit karta hai, INIT exit karta hai, namespace ka last process gaya toh mount namespace aur uske saare mounts kernel khud hata deta hai. Host side par cleanup() ke liye <state>/upper, work, merged ab sirf plain directories hain, toh shutil.rmtree(state) kaafi hai. Safety check: agar merged phir bhi host namespace mein mount dikhe (os.path.ismount) toh RuntimeError -- kabhi mounted overlay ke neeche rmtree mat karo. Upper delete = container ke saare changes gaye; test_image_rootfs_is_unchanged_after_many_runs aur test_two_containers_do_not_see_each_others_writes yeh prove karte hain.

Deletion ka format: container ke andar 'rm /etc/motd' karo toh overlayfs lower ki file chhupane ke liye upper/etc/motd par apna WHITEOUT banata hai: ek character device jiska major/minor 0/0 hai. test_deletion_is_recorded_as_an_overlay_whiteout container chalu rakhte hue (read x) upper ko lstat karke S_ISCHR aur rdev 0/0 assert karta hai. Yeh image layer ke '.wh.motd' format se ALAG hai. Docker jaise tools layer commit karte waqt 0/0 device ko .wh. mein badalte hain aur per-layer lowerdir use karte waqt ulta. minibox layers ko pull time par hi flatten karta hai, toh overlay ko kabhi .wh. files dikhti hi nahi -- dono formats kabhi milte nahi.
why_needed: Container ke mounts host par leak na hon aur crash ke baad bhi host mount table saaf rahe, plus deletes ka sahi semantics.
real_world_analogy: Hotel room ki temporary partition: guest checkout kare toh partition (mount namespace) apne aap gir jaati hai; staff ko sirf kachra (upper dir) uthana hai.
how_it_works: Mount namespace per container; last process exit -> kernel unmount. Overlay delete -> upper mein 0/0 char device whiteout (ya opaque dir xattr).
in_this_project: mounts.build_plan (step 1 private, step 2 overlay), container.init_main plan apply karta hai, container.cleanup (ismount check + rmtree), tests/integration/test_overlay.py.
code_example:
# real, minibox/container.py cleanup (trimmed)
if state and os.path.isdir(state):
    # The overlay itself lived only in INIT's mount namespace, which died with INIT, so these are
    # plain directories now. Deleting upper is what makes the container's changes disappear.
    merged = os.path.join(state, "merged")
    if os.path.ismount(merged):  # pragma: no cover - only if someone mounted it in the host ns
        raise RuntimeError(f"{merged} is still mounted in the host namespace")
    shutil.rmtree(state)
advantages: Kernel khud unmount karta hai, host mount table saaf
Cleanup = rmtree
Overlay whiteouts aur layer whiteouts kabhi mix nahi
disadvantages: minibox SIGKILL ho jaaye toh state dir reh jaata hai (koi gc nahi)
Container ke changes save/commit karne ka koi raasta nahi
common_mistakes: Overlay host namespace mein mount karna
Mounted merged ke neeche rmtree chalana
Overlay 0/0 whiteout aur .wh. ko same samajhna

Opaque directory overlayfs upper mein kaise represent hoti hai?

question: A malicious layer can contain a symlink 'link -> /somewhere/outside', and a later layer writes 'link/pwned'. How does _inside stop this, why only the PARENT directories, and why are absolute symlinks still kept?
answer_hinglish:
clean_member_path sirf naam dekhta hai; 'link/pwned' mein koi '..' nahi, toh naam-check pass. Lekin filesystem par 'link' ek symlink hai jo rootfs ke bahar point karta hai -- likhoge toh file host par jaayegi. Yeh attack multi-layer hai: layer 0 symlink rakhta hai, layer 1 uske through likhta hai. Isliye check filesystem ki CURRENT state par hona chahiye, naam par nahi.

_inside(root, rel): path = root/rel; parent = os.path.realpath(dirname(path)) -- yeh saare symlinks resolve kar deta hai; real_root = realpath(root). parent == real_root ya real_root + os.sep se shuru hona chahiye, warna UnsafePath('resolves outside the rootfs (through a symlink)'). Yeh har regular entry ke extract se pehle AUR har whiteout delete se pehle (apply_whiteout) chalta hai.

Sirf PARENT kyun: aakhri component khud ek symlink ho sakta hai aur yeh legit hai -- usko hum replace karte hain (_remove pehle unlink karta hai, symlink follow nahi karta: os.path.islink check). Agar poora path realpath karte, toh 'bin/sh -> /bin/busybox' jaise har absolute symlink ka resolve host ke /bin/busybox par hota aur galat reject ho jaata.

Absolute symlinks as-is rakhe jaate hain (test_absolute_symlinks_are_kept_as_is): image mein /bin/sh -> /bin/busybox hai, aur woh CONTAINER ke andar pivot_root ke baad resolve hota hai, jahan / = image root. Problem tabhi hai jab HOST side ka code (yeh puller) unke through likhe -- woh _inside rokta hai.

Tests: test_symlink_in_layer_cannot_redirect_a_later_file_outside, test_whiteout_through_symlink_outside_is_refused (outside/victim bachta hai). Mutation M27 (parent symlink check hata do) -> 2 red. Dono tests Windows par skip (symlinks privileges).
why_needed: Puller root ke roop mein chalta hai; ek symlink trick se host ki koi bhi file overwrite ya delete ho sakti hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ke andar ek darwaza jo seedha padosi ke ghar khulta hai (symlink). Saaman rakhne se pehle check karo ki jis kamre mein rakh rahe ho woh sach mein apne ghar mein hai -- darwaze ke paar nahi.
how_it_works: realpath(dirname(target)) ko realpath(root) prefix se compare. Prefix compare root + os.sep ke saath, taaki '/img/rootfs2' galti se '/img/rootfs' ke andar na maana jaaye.
in_this_project: image.py _inside, apply_whiteout, apply_layer, _remove; tarfile.tar_filter bhi destination ke bahar jaate links refuse karta hai (extra layer).
code_example:
# real, minibox/image.py
def _inside(root: str, rel: str) -> str:
    """root/rel, refusing it if a symlink in rel's PARENT directories points outside root."""
    path = os.path.join(root, *rel.split("/")) if rel else root
    parent = os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(path))
    real_root = os.path.realpath(root)
    if parent != real_root and not parent.startswith(real_root + os.sep):
        raise UnsafePath(f"{rel!r} resolves outside the rootfs (through a symlink)")
    return path
advantages: Multi-layer symlink attacks pakde jaate hain

question: Why does minibox wrap tarfile's 'tar' filter in _keep_mode instead of using it directly, and why does it extract with numeric_owner=True?
answer_hinglish:
Python 3.12 tarfile extraction filters deta hai: 'fully_trusted', 'tar', 'data'. 'tar' filter useful checks karta hai: absolute names refuse, destination ke bahar jaate paths/links refuse. Lekin woh mode bits bhi 'saaf' karta hai: setuid/setgid/sticky bits aur group/other write bits hata deta hai. Normal archive ke liye yeh safe default hai, lekin ek OS image ke liye galat: alpine ka /tmp 1777 (sticky + world-writable) hai. Filter ke baad woh 0755 ban jaata, aur container mein non-root user /tmp mein likh hi nahi paata.

_keep_mode(member, dest): checked = tarfile.tar_filter(member, dest) -- saari safety checks chalti hain, kuch galat ho toh exception wahi uthata hai -- phir checked.replace(mode=member.mode, deep=False) se image ka ASLI mode wapas. Yaani 'tarfile ki checks rakho, uski mode policy nahi'. apply_layer isse tf.extract(m, root, numeric_owner=True, filter=_keep_mode) mein deta hai.

Test test_sticky_and_world_writable_modes_survive ek DIRTYPE 'tmp' mode 0o1777 ke saath banata hai aur extract ke baad S_IMODE == 0o1777 check karta hai (Windows par skip). Mutation M28 ('tar filter used as is') ne 1 test red kiya -- aur README note karta hai ki test_minimal_dev bhi us run mein include tha.

numeric_owner=True: tar mein uid/gid number aur uname/gname dono hote hain. Default tarfile pehle naam ko HOST ke /etc/passwd mein dhundhta hai. Image ka 'root' ya 'nobody' host par alag uid ho sakta hai (ya koi image-specific user host par exist hi na kare). Image ke andar ke numbers image ke apne /etc/passwd ke hisaab se hain, toh numbers as-is rakhna hi sahi hai. Ownership sirf root hi set kar sakta hai, isliye SERVER_RUN mein note hai: alpine 'pulled again as root so the rootfs has uid 0 owners'.
why_needed: Image ka filesystem metadata (modes, owners) container ke behaviour ka hissa hai; galat mode ya owner se programs toot jaate hain ya security badal jaati hai.
real_world_analogy: Customs officer (tar_filter) bag check kare ki koi hathiyaar nahi -- theek. Lekin woh har dabba repack karke label bhi badal de, yeh nahi chahiye. Toh check uska, packing aapki original.
how_it_works: tar_filter returns a new TarInfo (ya raise); TarInfo.replace(mode=...) ek copy deta hai original mode ke saath; extract us filtered member ko use karta hai. numeric_owner se chown(uid, gid) seedhe numbers se.
in_this_project: image.py _keep_mode (comment ke saath), apply_layer extract call; test_image.py::test_sticky_and_world_writable_modes_survive; SERVER_RUN.md timeline 17:59:08.
code_example:
# real, minibox/image.py
def _keep_mode(member: tarfile.TarInfo, dest: str) -> tarfile.TarInfo:
    # tarfile's 'tar' filter refuses absolute names and paths that leave dest through symlinks
    # (what we want), but it also clears setuid/sticky and group/other write bits, which would
    # turn the image's 1777 /tmp into 0755. Keep its checks, restore the image's real mode.
    checked = tarfile.tar_filter(member, dest)
    return checked.replace(mode=member.mode, deep=False)

Image ka exact mode aur owner preserve
Chhota, readable wrapper
disadvantages: setuid binaries bhi preserve hote hain -- image ke andar se privilege escalation possible (aur yeh security boundary nahi hai)
Non-root pull par ownership set nahi hoti
common_mistakes: 'data' ya 'tar' filter as-is use karna (1777 /tmp toot jaata hai)
filter='fully_trusted' (koi checks nahi)
Owner names ko host par resolve karna
follow_up_questions: Non-root user ke roop mein pull karna ho toh ownership kaise preserve karoge (user namespace, xattrs)?
setuid bits preserve karna kab risky hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Stdlib filter ko wrap karna vs apni checks likhna: wrap se tested checks milti hain aur hamara code sirf mode policy badalta hai. Cost: Python ke internal filter behaviour par depend, aur setuid preserve karne ka matlab image ke setuid binaries host par root-owned setuid files ban jaati hain (rootfs dir mein).
advanced.failure_scenarios: 1) Filter as-is: /tmp 0755, non-root app crash (M28). 2) numeric_owner=False: image ka uid 1000 'app' user host par missing -> tarfile fallback ya galat owner. 3) Non-root pull: chown fail/skip, sab files pulling user ki -- container ke andar root ke roop mein chalega lekin owners galat.
advanced.alternatives: Apna minimal filter likhna (names, links, devices), filter='data' + manual chmod pass, ya umoci/containerd jaisa unpacker. Rootless setups mein ownership ko user xattrs (fuse-overlayfs) ya idmapped mounts se represent karna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Owner/mode handling per entry constant cost hai; scale par asli issue setuid files ka host disk par root-owned reh jaana aur kai images ke duplicate copies hain -- shared content store + idmapped mounts better.
advanced.production_improvements: Host par rootfs directory ko 0700 parent ke andar rakhna (taaki host users setuid binaries tak na pahunchein), nosuid mount options jahan possible, device nodes in layers ko refuse ya whitelist karna, aur rootless mode ke liye user namespace mapping.

question: minibox verifies every blob before applying ANY layer. Walk through the order of operations in pull() and explain what guarantee this gives when something goes wrong.
answer_hinglish:
pull() ka order deliberately 'pehle sab verify, phir sab apply' hai:

1) parse_reference -> Registry.
2) reg.manifest(ref): tag par Docker-Content-Digest check (agar header hai), digest par strict check.
3) Index hai toh select_platform -> manifest BY DIGEST (strict check). Media type MANIFEST_TYPES mein nahi -> RegistryError.
4) Config blob download + _verify_blob(config digest). Config parse, len(diff_ids) == len(layers) warna error.
5) Har layer: media type gzip/plain hona chahiye (zstd -> RegistryError), download, compressed digest, size, diff_id (decompressed). Fail -> blob delete + raise.
6) SIRF ab: rootfs rmtree + makedirs, saari layers apply_layer, manifest.json + config.json likho, summary return.

Guarantee: koi bhi verification fail ho, toh rootfs directory banti hi nahi -- 'half-built rootfs' jisme 2 layers sahi aur teesri tampered ho, kabhi nahi milega. test_tampered_content_is_refused_and_nothing_is_applied teeno cases (layer, config, manifest) mein assert karta hai ki DigestMismatch aaya AUR tmp/img/rootfs exist nahi karta. Verified blobs disk par reh jaate hain (woh sahi hain), failed blob delete.

Yeh kyun important: apply_layer root ke roop mein untrusted tar ko filesystem par likhta hai. Tar parsing khud attack surface hai. Verification ke baad hum kam se kam itna jaante hain ki yeh wahi bytes hain jo manifest/config ne commit kiye the. Honest limitation: apply step khud atomic nahi hai -- agar verified layer apply ke beech UnsafePath ('..', symlink escape) se fail ho, toh rootfs adhoora reh jaata hai (purana rootfs pehle hi rmtree ho chuka). Behtar: temp directory mein apply karke end mein rename.
why_needed: Integrity failure ko 'kuch nahi hua' state mein badalna, taaki koi galti se aadha/tampered rootfs container ka root na ban jaaye.
real_world_analogy: Building material site par aane par pehle har truck ka challan aur maal check, sab theek ho tabhi construction shuru. Beech mein ek truck kharab nikla toh aadhi deewar nahi khadi hoti.
how_it_works: Two-phase: fetch+verify phase (side effects sirf blobs dir tak), apply phase (rootfs). Phase 1 ke errors phase 2 shuru hi nahi hone dete.
in_this_project: registry.py pull() (module docstring step 5 aur 6: 'Nothing is applied until everything is verified'), _verify_blob; test_registry.py tamper tests.

rootfs = os.path.join(dest, "rootfs")
if os.path.exists(rootfs):
    shutil.rmtree(rootfs)
os.makedirs(rootfs)
counts = [image.apply_layer(p, rootfs) for p in layer_paths]
with open(os.path.join(dest, "manifest.json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(doc, f, indent=1)

Failure ka clear state: rootfs nahi bana
Tests mein assert karna aasaan
disadvantages: Saari layers pehle download honi chahiye (disk space, latency -- pipelining nahi)
Apply phase khud atomic nahi
Purana rootfs pehle hi delete
common_mistakes: Download karte karte apply karna (stream) bina verify
Verify fail par blob rakhe rehna
Sochna ki verification tar ke andar ke attacks bhi rokti hai
follow_up_questions: Apply ko atomic kaise banaoge (temp dir + rename)?
Bade images ke liye download aur verify ko parallel kaise karoge bina guarantee tode?
Verified hone ke baad bhi tar safety checks kyun chahiye?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Simplicity aur strong guarantee vs latency: sab download+verify pehle, isliye bade images mein apply tab shuru hota hai jab aakhri layer aa jaaye. Docker/containerd layers parallel download aur per-layer unpack karte hain (har layer verify hone ke baad apne snapshot mein) -- woh bhi 'verify before use' hai, bas per layer.
advanced.failure_scenarios: 1) Layer 2 ka digest mismatch: blob delete, rootfs nahi bana, DigestMismatch. 2) Config tampered: config delete, koi layer download hi nahi. 3) diff_ids order galat: layers sahi download, diff_id fail. 4) Verified layer mein '..' member: UnsafePath beech apply mein, rootfs adhoora (aur purana gaya). 5) Network beech mein toot: .part file reh jaati hai, rootfs untouched.
advanced.alternatives: Per-layer snapshots (containerd snapshotter): har layer verify hokar apne dir mein unpack, image tab ready jab saari ho jaayein. Ya temp rootfs + atomic rename. Ya streaming hash + unpack into temp, verify end par, fail par temp delete.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x layers: sequential download latency dominate karegi -> parallel downloads (verify per blob). 100x images: shared blob store + per-layer snapshots se dedupe; verify ek baar per blob, phir cache se.
advanced.production_improvements: Apply ko temp dir mein karke rename, purana rootfs tab tak rakhna, .part files ka resume/cleanup, parallel downloads, aur download size ko manifest size par cap karna (bahut bada blob disk na bhare).

question: minibox flattens all layers into one directory and uses it as a single overlay lowerdir. Docker uses one lowerdir per layer. Compare the two designs.
answer_hinglish:
minibox ka decision (PLAN.md): pull time par saari layers order mein ek directory <dest>/rootfs mein apply, whiteouts usi waqt OCI format (.wh.) mein resolve, aur yeh directory overlay ka EK read-only lowerdir. Container ke liye options string sirf 'lowerdir=<rootfs>,upperdir=..,workdir=..'.

Fayde:
- Simple: overlay ko kabhi .wh. files ya multiple lowers nahi dikhte; layer whiteouts aur overlay ke 0/0 device whiteouts kabhi mix nahi hote.
- Whiteouts ek baar apply, plain Python file ops se -- unit testable Windows par bhi.
- Lookup ek hi lower mein, mount options chhote (overlay_options ':' wale paths refuse karta hai; multi-lower mein ':' separator hota).

Nuksaan:
- Koi sharing nahi: do images jo same base layer use karti hain, disk par do full copies. README NOT-done list yahi kehti hai.
- Har pull poora rootfs dobara banata hai (rmtree + apply), incremental update nahi.
- Layer boundaries khatam: baad mein 'kaunsi file kis layer se' ya ek layer replace karna possible nahi.

Docker ka overlay2: har layer apni directory mein unpack, image = lowerdir=L3:L2:L1 (upar se neeche). Layer whiteouts unpack ke waqt overlay format (0/0 char device, opaque ke liye xattr) mein convert hote hain taaki overlay unhe samjhe. Fayda: layers images ke beech shared, pull mein sirf nayi layers. Cost: lowerdir limits (mount options page size, layer count), conversion code, aur zyada complex GC (refcount per layer).

Interview line: learning runtime ke liye flatten sahi trade-off hai -- correctness aur testability pehle; storage efficiency ko jaan-boojh kar chhoda aur honestly document kiya.
why_needed: Yeh decision storage, pull speed, whiteout handling aur GC sabko affect karta hai; samajhna zaroori hai ki kya kis keemat par mila.
real_world_analogy: Ek book ke kai revisions: ek tarika har revision ko merge karke ek final copy chhapna (flatten); doosra original + har revision ke patches transparent sheets ki tarah rakhna (per-layer), jisse doosri books bhi same sheets use kar sakein.
how_it_works: Flatten: N layers -> 1 dir (pull time cost O(total files)). Per-layer: N dirs, overlay runtime par stack karta hai; whiteouts kernel format mein.
in_this_project: PLAN.md Images decision, README 'NOT implemented' (layers flattened), mounts.overlay_options, mounts.build_plan (overlay.lower must be the rootfs), image.apply_layer.
advantages: Simple aur testable
Ek whiteout format per stage
Ek lowerdir, chhota mount option
disadvantages: Disk par koi dedupe nahi
Har pull full rebuild
Layer identity kho jaati hai
common_mistakes: Flattened dir mein .wh. files chhod dena (overlay unhe normal files samjhega)
Per-layer lowerdir mein .wh. ko convert na karna
Lowerdir order ulta dena (overlay mein pehla = sabse upar)
follow_up_questions: Per-layer lowerdirs par migrate karna ho toh apply_layer mein kya badlega?
Overlay ke lowerdir count/size limits kya problem create karte hain?
Shared layers ka GC kaise design karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Flatten = correctness, simplicity, single whiteout format; per-layer = disk dedupe, faster incremental pulls, but conversion of whiteouts to overlay format, multi-lower mount limits, refcounted GC. minibox ka goal learning + honest tests tha, isliye flatten.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Flatten: bade images ka har pull minutes le sakta hai aur disk double; ek layer apply fail -> poora rootfs adhoora. Per-layer: whiteout conversion bug -> deleted files wapas dikhna; bahut zyada layers -> mount option limit exceed, mount fail; GC bug -> in-use layer delete.
advanced.alternatives: containerd snapshotters (overlayfs, native), fuse-overlayfs (rootless), lazy-pulling snapshotters (stargz) jo layers on-demand fetch karte hain, ya composefs/erofs based images.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x images same base par: flatten = 10 full copies; per-layer = base ek baar. 100x containers ek image par: dono designs mein lowerdir share hota hai (minibox mein bhi ek rootfs, kai upper dirs), toh container scale par flatten bhi theek hai; image scale par nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-layer unpack dirs keyed by diff_id, refcount/GC, whiteout conversion to overlay char devices + trusted.overlay.opaque xattr, lowerdir stacking with limit checks, aur image metadata store jo tag -> manifest -> layers map rakhe.

question: The README says 'a TAG is a mutable name'. What exactly does minibox's verification prove for 'alpine:3.20' versus 'alpine@sha256:...', and what does it not prove?
answer_hinglish:
Verification chain samjho ki kahan se 'trust anchor' shuru hota hai.

alpine@sha256:<D> (digest ref): parse_reference digest rakhta hai, Reference.ref digest return karta hai, Registry.manifest check karta hai ki index/manifest bytes ka sha256 == D. Uske baad har link digest se: chosen platform manifest (by digest), config (digest), layers (digest + size), content (diff_id). Matlab agar aapne D kisi bharosemand source se liya (release notes, apni CI), toh registry, CDN, proxy -- koi bhi beech mein badle, pull fail hoga. Yeh END-TO-END verification hai.

alpine:3.20 (tag): pehla document tag se aata hai. Uske against independent hash nahi hai; minibox sirf Docker-Content-Digest header (agar present) se compare karta hai, jo wahi server bhejta hai jo body bhejta hai. Yeh corruption/truncation pakadta hai, tampering nahi. Toh trust anchor hai 'Docker Hub ne TLS par jo bheja'. Uske neeche ka sab kuch (platform manifest se layers tak) phir bhi digest-verified hai -- matlab registry ek consistent image dega, lekin KAUNSI image, yeh registry decide karti hai. Aur tag mutable hai: kal 3.20 kisi aur digest par point kar sakta hai.

Kya prove NAHI hota: publisher authenticity (koi signature verification nahi -- cosign/notation jaisa kuch nahi), freshness/rollback protection (purana vulnerable digest bhi valid hai), aur image ka content safe hai (verified malicious image bhi verified hai). Aur yaad rakho: minibox security boundary nahi hai -- container root hai, capabilities sab hain, toh image trust aur bhi important hai: 'Run only code you would run as root on the host anyway.'

Practical advice: production mein digest pin karo (summary mein manifest_digest aur index_digest log hote hain -- unhe record karke agli baar by digest pull karo).
why_needed: Integrity aur authenticity alag cheezein hain; interview mein yeh farak saaf batana zaroori hai.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan se 'is hafte ka special' (tag) maangna vs 'item code 4471' (digest) maangna. Item code se aapko wahi milega jo aapne note kiya tha; 'special' dukaandaar decide karta hai -- dabba sealed hoga, lekin kaunsa dabba, unki marzi.
how_it_works: Trust anchor = pehla hash jo aapke paas pehle se hai. Digest ref: anchor aapke haath mein. Tag ref: anchor registry ka response (TLS).
in_this_project: registry.py Registry.manifest (dono branches aur comment), parse_reference digest regex, pull() summary (index_digest, manifest_digest); README 'Trust note'.

Digest pinning ke saath security updates kaise milenge?

Signatures add karna extra dependency aur key management hai jo stdlib-only scope se bahar tha.
advanced.failure_scenarios: 1) Registry compromise + tag repoint: tag pull naya (malicious) image verify karke de dega. Digest pull fail. 2) CDN ne layer badla: dono modes mein fail (layer digest). 3) TLS MITM with bad CA: tag pull ko jhootha index mil sakta hai; digest pull fail. 4) Purana vulnerable digest pin: verify pass, vuln andar.

question: Coding exercise: implement apply_layer(tar_path, root) that applies one OCI layer with whiteouts, path safety and the image's real modes. Then compare with minibox's version.
answer_hinglish:
Interview mein approach pehle bolo, phir code:

1) tarfile.open(path, 'r:*') -- gzip aur plain dono auto-detect.
2) Har member ka naam normalise + '..' reject (clean_member_path). Bad naam par poori layer refuse karo, skip nahi -- attacker ka layer hai.
3) classify: '.wh..wh..opq' -> opaque(parent), '.wh.X' -> file(parent/X), baaki normal. '.wh.' aur '.wh...' reject.
4) PASS 1: whiteouts turant apply (sirf lower layers ka content abhi rootfs mein hai). Delete se pehle _inside check (parent symlink bahar na jaaye). File whiteout: symlink/file unlink, dir rmtree. Opaque: dir ke children delete, dir khud rahe.
5) PASS 2: regular entries. Target ka parent _inside se check. Agar existing entry type badal rahi hai (file <-> dir) toh pehle remove; dir par dir ho toh merge (remove mat karo, warna lower ke children jaayenge). Hardlink linkname bhi clean karo.
6) Extract with numeric_owner=True aur filter jo tar_filter ki checks rakhe lekin original mode restore kare (1777 /tmp).
7) Counts return karo (whiteouts, opaque, entries) -- tests aur logs ke liye.

minibox ka image.apply_layer exactly yeh hai (neeche code). Test cases jo interviewer poochega: opaque marker tar mein file ke BAAD (file bachni chahiye), same-layer re-add, missing whiteout target harmless, file->dir->file replacement, '../evil' aur '../.wh.victim' refused, symlink-then-write refused, 1777 preserved. minibox mein yeh sab tests/unit/test_image.py mein hain, aur mutations M23-M28 inhi se pakde gaye.
why_needed: Layer application container image handling ka core hai aur ismein ordering + security dono ek saath sochne padte hain -- achha interview exercise.
real_world_analogy: Pehle purane saaman ki list se cheezein hatao, phir naya saaman rakho, aur har cheez rakhne se pehle dekho ki kamra apne ghar ka hai.
how_it_works: Two-pass loop over getmembers(), safety checks per entry, extract with custom filter.
in_this_project: image.py apply_layer, clean_member_path, classify, apply_whiteout, _inside, _keep_mode, _remove.
code_example:
# real, minibox/image.py apply_layer
def apply_layer(tar_path: str, root: str) -> dict:
    os.makedirs(root, exist_ok=True)
    counts = {"whiteouts": 0, "opaque": 0, "entries": 0}
    with tarfile.open(tar_path, "r:*") as tf:
        members = tf.getmembers()
        regular = []
        for m in members:
            rel = clean_member_path(m.name)
            wh = classify(rel)
            if wh is None:
                if rel:
                    regular.append((rel, m))
                continue
            apply_whiteout(root, wh)
            counts["whiteouts" if wh.kind == "file" else "opaque"] += 1
        for rel, m in regular:
            path = _inside(root, rel)
            # A layer may replace a dir with a file or the other way round; tarfile won't.
            if os.path.lexists(path) and not (m.isdir() and os.path.isdir(path) and not os.path.islink(path)):
                _remove(path)
            m.name = rel
            if m.islnk():
                m.linkname = clean_member_path(m.linkname)
            tf.extract(m, root, numeric_owner=True, filter=_keep_mode)
            counts["entries"] += 1
    return counts

Har escape path covered (naam, symlink, whiteout)
Counts se observability

Dir par dir aaye toh bhi remove kar dena (lower children kho jaate)
Bad member ko skip karke aage badhna
