Device node entries (block devices) ke saath kya karna chahiye?
Is function ke liye property-based test kaise likhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Correctness (two-pass) vs memory (getmembers list). Python tarfile gzip stream ko seek karke dobara padh sakta hai; ek pass streaming design ke liye whiteouts ko buffer karna padta (ya per-layer dirs jahan order matter nahi karta).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Opaque marker baad mein + single pass -> same-layer files delete (M25). Dir-on-dir remove -> lower layer ke children gayab. Hardlink linkname unclean -> link bahar ki file se. Filter as-is -> /tmp 0755 (M28).
advanced.alternatives: Per-layer unpack (har layer apni dir, overlay stacking) jahan whiteouts overlay format mein convert hote hain; Go ka containerd archive package; umoci unpack.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade layers (GBs, lakhon entries): getmembers memory badhega aur realpath per entry; streaming + openat2 dirfd-based extraction better. Bahut images: parallel apply per layer in per-layer design.
advanced.production_improvements: Streaming extraction, device-node policy, extraction in unprivileged sandbox, aur fuzz tests (random tar members + invariant: kuch bhi root ke bahar na bane).

question: List the ways 'minibox pull' can fail (network, auth, platform, media types, verification, tar safety). For each, what does the user see and what state is left on disk?
answer_hinglish:
pull ke failure modes, order mein, aur disk state:

1) Bad reference ('Alpine', 'alpine@sha256:xyz', 'alpine:bad tag'): parse_reference ValueError -- network call bhi nahi, disk par kuch nahi.
2) Auth: challenge Basic ho -> RegistryError('unsupported auth scheme'); realm missing -> error; token endpoint non-200 ya token absent -> RegistryError. Disk par kuch nahi.
3) Unknown tag: manifests/<tag> 404 -> RegistryError('GET ...: HTTP 404') (test_unknown_tag_is_an_error). Kuch nahi bana.
4) Manifest too large (> 4 MiB) ya digest/Docker-Content-Digest mismatch -> RegistryError / DigestMismatch, abhi tak blobs dir bhi nahi bani.
5) Platform na mile: RegistryError('no manifest for linux/riscv64 in index (have: ...)') (test_wrong_platform_is_a_clear_error).
6) Unsupported manifest media type (jaise purana schema1) -> RegistryError.
7) Config mismatch -> config blob delete, DigestMismatch. len(diff_ids) != len(layers) -> RegistryError.
8) Layer media type zstd ya kuch aur -> RegistryError('only tar and tar+gzip'). Pehle ke verified blobs disk par rehte hain.
9) Layer digest, size ya diff_id fail -> woh blob delete (test_failed_blob_is_deleted_not_cached), rootfs nahi bana (test_tampered_content_...).
10) Network beech mein toota: urllib exception ya short body; .part file reh jaati hai, final blob nahi. Agla pull .part ko overwrite karega.
11) Verified layer apply ke beech UnsafePath ('..', symlink escape, bad whiteout): rootfs ADHOORA reh jaata hai -- verify-before-apply yahan cover nahi karta.

CLI: cli.main pull mein exceptions catch nahi hote, toh user ko Python traceback dikhta hai with clear message (RegistryError/DigestMismatch/UnsafePath ka text). Honest: yeh polished UX nahi hai; exit code bhi non-zero traceback wala hai, run ke 125 jaisa mapping nahi.
why_needed: Production mein failures ka matlab hai 'kya state bachi' -- operator ko pata hona chahiye retry safe hai ya cleanup chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Courier delivery ke failure modes: galat address (reference), gate pass nahi mila (auth), item stock mein nahi (404), galat size (platform), damaged parcel (digest) -- har case mein ghar mein kya pada hai, yeh alag hai.
how_it_works: Exceptions RegistryError / DigestMismatch / UnsafePath / ValueError; disk side effects sirf blobs dir (verified blobs + .part) aur aakhri phase mein rootfs.
in_this_project: registry.py pull, Registry.get, Registry.manifest, select_platform, _verify_blob; image.py UnsafePath; cli.py main; test_registry.py failure tests.
code_example:
# real, minibox/registry.py pull (trimmed)
lt = layer.get("mediaType", "")
if lt not in GZIP_LAYER_TYPES + PLAIN_LAYER_TYPES:
    raise RegistryError(f"layer {i}: unsupported media type {lt!r} (only tar and tar+gzip)")
...
if len(diff_ids) != len(doc["layers"]):
    raise RegistryError(f"{len(doc['layers'])} layers but {len(diff_ids)} diff_ids in the config")
advantages: Har failure ka specific message
Tampered/failed blobs disk par nahi bachte
Verification failures rootfs nahi banate
disadvantages: Apply-phase failure rootfs adhoora chhodta hai
CLI traceback deta hai, clean exit code nahi
Token expiry, retries, resume nahi
common_mistakes: Network error par automatic retry bina limit
Failure ke baad .part ko valid blob samajhna
Error message mein available platforms na dikhana
follow_up_questions: Retry/backoff kaunse errors par safe hai aur kaunse par nahi?
Apply-phase failure ke baad recovery kaise automatic banaoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Fail-fast + clear exceptions vs resilience: minibox har error par turant ruk jaata hai, koi retry nahi. Simple aur predictable, lekin flaky network par bade pulls baar baar shuru se (verified blobs reuse hote hain, toh poora nahi).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Flaky CDN: beech mein toot, .part reh jaati hai. Docker Hub rate limit (429): 'HTTP 429' error, koi backoff nahi. Token expire on bade layer: second 401 -> error. Disk full during apply: OSError, rootfs adhoora.
advanced.alternatives: containerd/skopeo: retries with backoff, resumable downloads (Range requests), per-layer status, content store ingest with partial commit, aur clear exit codes.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x pulls ek saath: rate limits jaldi lagenge -> shared cache/mirror. 100x: pull-through registry mirror, concurrency limit, aur metrics (failure type counts).
advanced.production_improvements: Error -> exit code mapping CLI mein, retry with backoff sirf network/5xx/429 par (digest mismatch par kabhi nahi), Range-based resume for .part, temp rootfs + rename, aur structured logs with digest per step.

question: What do overlay_options' refusal of ',' and ':' and build_plan's 'overlay.lower must be the rootfs' check protect against, and how does mutation M19 show that the overlay (not a bind mount) is what keeps the image clean?
answer_hinglish:
build_plan(rootfs, overlay=None, mount_proc=True) ka step 2 root filesystem decide karta hai:

- overlay diya (default, cfg.overlay True): Mount('overlay', overlay.merged, 'overlay', 0, overlay_options(overlay)), aur new_root = overlay.merged. Container ka / merged view hai; writes upper mein.
- --no-overlay (cli mein dest='overlay', action='store_false'): Mount(rootfs, rootfs, None, MS_BIND|MS_REC) -- rootfs ko KHUD par bind mount. new_root = rootfs. Kyun? pivot_root(new_root, put_old) ki shart hai ki new_root ek mount point ho. Ek normal directory mount point nahi hoti; khud par bind mount usse mount point bana deta hai bina kuch copy kiye. Is mode mein writes seedhe --rootfs mein jaate hain aur bachte hain: test_no_overlay_writes_into_the_rootfs image ki COPY par chalta hai, /root/persisted 'kept' check karta hai, aur yeh bhi ki .oldroot (pivot_root ka put_old) baad mein hata diya gaya.

Checks:
1) build_plan: overlay hai aur abspath(overlay.lower) != abspath(rootfs) -> ValueError('overlay.lower must be the rootfs'). Plan ke baaki steps (proc, dev) new_root ke andar paths banate hain; lower aur rootfs alag hon toh caller ki galti silently galat image chala sakti thi.
2) overlay_options: lower/upper/work mein ',' ya ':' ho toh ValueError. Mount data string mein ',' options alag karta hai aur ':' multiple lowerdirs -- aisa path dusre option inject kar sakta hai ya galat lower bana sakta hai. Escaping rules hain, lekin refuse karna simple aur safe.

Mutation M19 (overlay ki jagah image ka bind mount) ne 5 mein se 4 overlay tests red kiye -- writes image mein chale gaye. Plan data hai (Mount/Mkdir/Mknod/Symlink dataclasses), toh order aur flags tests/unit/test_mounts.py mein kisi bhi OS par test hote hain.
why_needed: Root filesystem ka sahi mount pivot_root ke liye prerequisite hai, aur mount option strings injection ka source ban sakti hain.
real_world_analogy: Stage par play: ya toh asli set (rootfs) par transparent sheets (overlay), ya asli set hi istemaal (no-overlay) -- lekin dono mein stage ko 'officially stage' declare karna padta hai (mount point), warna director (pivot_root) shuru nahi karta.
how_it_works: Plan steps list: [private /, root mount, proc, dev..., Mkdir .oldroot]; apply_plan INIT mein execute; enter_root pivot_root karta hai.
in_this_project: mounts.py build_plan, overlay_options, OverlayDirs, enter_root; cli.py --no-overlay; container.py run (OverlayDirs banana); tests test_mounts.py aur test_overlay.py.
advantages: Ek hi code path, do modes
Plan data hai -> unit testable
Option injection refuse
disadvantages: --no-overlay image ko permanently badal deta hai
',' ya ':' wale legit paths support nahi
common_mistakes: pivot_root ko normal directory par chalana (EINVAL)
Mount options string mein user paths bina validate
--no-overlay ko shared image par chalana
follow_up_questions: Read-only rootfs (docker --read-only) is plan mein kaise jodoge?
--no-overlay ka use case kya hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Overlay default (safe, disposable) vs no-overlay (persistent, debugging/image prep). Plan-as-data se dono modes ek function mein, aur order unit test hota hai. Reject-instead-of-escape for ',' ':' trades flexibility for safety.
advanced.failure_scenarios: 1) M19: image bind mount -> container writes image mein (4 tests red). 2) State dir path mein ':' -> ValueError, exit 125. 3) Upper aur work alag filesystem -> kernel mount EINVAL. 4) --no-overlay par 'rm -rf' -> image permanently toota.
advanced.alternatives: Read-only bind (MS_RDONLY remount) for no-overlay, fsconfig/fsmount new mount API (Linux 5.2+) jahan options key-value calls hain (koi string parsing nahi, isliye ',' ':' issue nahi), ya tmpfs upper.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x containers ek image par: overlay mein lowerdir share, upper per container -- scale achha. Bahut sare mounts: har container apne namespace mein, host mount table par asar nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: fsmount API, read-only rootfs option, upper dir ko quota wale filesystem par (disk limit), aur state dir ka gc for crashed runs.

question: minibox has no image cache shared across pulls. Design a content-addressed store (blobs, per-layer snapshots, tag index, refcounts and GC) that would let many images and containers share layers safely.
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest baseline: aaj har 'minibox pull --dest X' apna blobs/sha256/<hex> aur flattened rootfs banata hai. Do images same alpine base use karein toh do copies; koi gc nahi; koi tag -> digest index nahi.

Design (containerd jaisa, lekin chhota):

TABLES (ek SQLite ya bbolt jaisa embedded store, plus files):
1) blobs(digest PK, size, media_type, state: ingesting|committed, created_at). Files: store/blobs/sha256/<hex>. Write: ingest/<random>.part -> hash streaming -> verify -> rename -> row committed. Minibox ka .part + os.replace + delete-on-fail pattern yahi hai, bas global.
2) images(name PK e.g. 'docker.io/library/alpine:3.20', target_digest, updated_at) -- tag ek mutable pointer, digest immutable.
3) manifests_children(parent_digest, child_digest) -- index -> manifest -> config/layers edges. GC ke liye graph.
4) snapshots(diff_id PK, parent_chain_id, path, state) -- har layer ek baar unpack, key = chain id (parent chain + diff_id ka hash, kyunki same layer alag parent par alag result deti hai whiteouts ki wajah se).
5) leases(container_id, snapshot_chain_id) / containers(id, upper_path) -- running containers kis snapshot par hain.

GC (mark and sweep): roots = images ke target digests + active leases. Graph walk se reachable blobs/snapshots mark. Baaki sweep, lekin grace period ke saath (ingesting blobs aur abhi-abhi bani images ko na hatao). Ek global lock ya 'gc generation' taaki pull aur gc race na karein (pull pehle lease leta hai, phir blobs likhta hai).

Mount: lowerdir = snapshot paths chain (upar se neeche), whiteouts unpack ke waqt overlay format (0/0 char device + opaque xattr) mein convert. Minibox ka overlay_options ':' refuse karta hai -- multi-lower mein ':' separator hai, toh paths controlled (store ke andar hex naam) honge.

Invariants: committed blob ka hash == naam (har read par optional re-verify), failed ingest kabhi committed nahi (minibox ka 'never cache a blob that failed'), snapshot tabhi ready jab uska diff_id verify ho chuka.
why_needed: Disk aur pull time scale karne ke liye layers share karni padti hain, aur sharing ke saath hi refcount/GC aur concurrency problems aate hain.
real_world_analogy: Library ka central godown: har book (blob) ek baar, catalogue (tag index) bataata hai kaunsa edition, issue register (leases) bataata hai kaun padh raha hai; saal mein ek baar jo kisi catalogue ya register mein nahi, woh hata do.
how_it_works: Content-addressed blobs + metadata DB of pointers and edges + leases; GC = reachability from roots; atomic ingest via temp + rename.
in_this_project: Aaj ka baseline: registry.py Registry.blob, _verify_blob, pull (per-dest store); image.apply_layer (flatten); README NOT-done ('No image cache across pulls', 'Layers are flattened').

# real, minibox/registry.py Registry.blob (today's per-pull store)
path = os.path.join(dest_dir, digest.split(":", 1)[1])
if not os.path.exists(path):
    tmp = path + ".part"
    self.get(f"{self.base}/blobs/{digest}", save_to=tmp)
    os.replace(tmp, path)
return path
advantages: Layers ek baar disk par
Pull sirf missing blobs
Tag/digest separation clear
disadvantages: GC aur leases ki complexity
Metadata DB aur files ke beech consistency
Chain ids aur whiteout conversion
common_mistakes: Snapshot ko sirf diff_id par key karna (parent chain ignore)
GC bina grace period (in-flight pull ke blobs delete)
Tag ko immutable maan kar cache karna
follow_up_questions: Pull aur GC ke beech race kaise rokoge?
Chain id kyun chahiye, sirf diff_id kyun nahi?
Crash ke baad DB aur disk ko reconcile kaise karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Embedded DB (SQLite/bbolt) metadata ke liye vs pure filesystem (symlinks/hardlinks as refs): DB transactions aur queries deta hai, filesystem-only simple hai lekin atomic multi-step updates mushkil. Mark-and-sweep vs refcount: refcount fast lekin crash par drift; mark-sweep slow lekin self-healing. Recommend: SQLite + mark-sweep with leases.
advanced.failure_scenarios: 1) GC in-flight pull ke blobs hata de -> pull fail ya corrupted snapshot. 2) Crash between rename aur DB row -> orphan file (GC sweep pakad leta hai). 3) Snapshot unpack crash -> state ingesting, restart par discard. 4) Running container ka lowerdir GC -> container ke andar ENOENT (leases yeh rokte hain). 5) Same blob do parallel pulls -> dono ingest, ek rename jeetega, same content toh safe.
advanced.alternatives: containerd content store + metadata (bbolt) + snapshotters; podman/c/storage (layers.json + overlay dirs); OCI image-layout directory (index.json + blobs) as a simple shared format; lazy pulling (stargz) for huge images.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x images same base: disk ~ base + deltas instead of 10x. 100x: GC time badhta hai (graph walk), toh incremental GC ya generation-based; metadata DB ek single writer -- pulls serialize ho sakte hain, isliye blob ingest outside lock, sirf commit inside.
advanced.production_improvements: Leases API, per-blob verify on read (optional), metrics (store size, reclaimable bytes), 'minibox images/rmi/gc' commands, dedupe across registries by digest, aur fsck command jo files vs DB reconcile kare.

question: The image config is downloaded but Env, Cmd, WorkingDir and User are ignored, layers must be tar or tar+gzip, and there is no push or build. Lay out how you would grow minibox's image support toward a docker-like runtime, in priority order.
answer_hinglish:
Pehle aaj ki state (README NOT-done): config.json dest mein save hota hai lekin run usse padhta nahi -- command, env, workdir user deta hai (container_env sirf PATH, HOME, HOSTNAME, TERM aur --env). Layers sirf GZIP_LAYER_TYPES ya PLAIN_LAYER_TYPES; zstd par RegistryError. Har pull complete, koi shared cache nahi. Push/build nahi. Yeh scope ki honest boundaries hain.

Priority order, aur kyun:

1) IMAGE CONFIG USE KARNA (sabse zyada user value, sabse kam risk). run ko --image DIR dena, config.json se Entrypoint + Cmd (user command Cmd override kare, docker semantics), Env (image env + --env override; PATH image ka), WorkingDir (cli ka --workdir override). User ko abhi IGNORE ya explicit error -- kyunki minibox mein user namespace nahi, aur 'User: 1000' ko setuid se implement karna bina capability dropping ke false sense of security dega. Yeh documented rehna chahiye.
2) ZSTD layers: application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+zstd. Stdlib mein zstd nahi tha (Python 3.14 mein compression.zstd aaya), toh ya dependency ya Python version bump. diff_id verify decompressed stream par same tarah.
3) SHARED STORE + per-layer snapshots (dekho blob store design), taaki images layers share karein; flatten ko per-layer lowerdirs se replace, whiteouts ko overlay format mein convert.
4) Lifecycle: minibox ps/stop/gc -- aaj minibox SIGKILL ho toh container aur state dir reh jaate hain.
5) PUSH (blob upload: POST/PUT uploads, monolithic ya chunked, phir manifest PUT) -- auth scope 'push'.
6) BUILD: sabse bada. Minimum: container chalao, upper dir ko layer tar banao (overlay 0/0 whiteouts -> .wh. files, opaque xattr -> .wh..wh..opq -- test_deletion_is_recorded_as_an_overlay_whiteout ne dikhaya ki upper mein exactly yahi format hai), diff_id + gzip digest compute, config mein diff_ids append, manifest likho.

Security ko is roadmap mein alag track rakhna: user namespace, cap drop, seccomp -- in ke bina image config ka 'User' bhi meaningful nahi. Stage 4 networking (veth) bhi alag track hai.
why_needed: Senior interview mein yeh dikhana ki aap scope ki seemayein jaante ho aur unhe value/risk ke hisaab se order kar sakte ho.
real_world_analogy: Ek chhota dhaba restaurant banana: pehle menu card (image config) follow karo, phir naye ingredients (zstd), phir central kitchen (shared store), aur catering (push/build) sabse aakhir mein.
how_it_works: Har step existing seams par baithta hai: config.json already saved, media type tuples registry.py mein, OverlayDirs/build_plan mounts mein, upper dir format already tested.
in_this_project: registry.py GZIP_LAYER_TYPES/PLAIN_LAYER_TYPES aur pull (config.json copy), container.py container_env, README NOT-done list, PLAN.md 'Not in scope'.
code_example:
# real, minibox/registry.py
GZIP_LAYER_TYPES = ("application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+gzip",
                    "application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.diff.tar.gzip")
PLAIN_LAYER_TYPES = ("application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar",)
advantages: Value-first ordering
Existing seams reuse
Security limitations explicit rakhe
disadvantages: Har step maintenance badhata hai
Build/push ke saath auth, retries, chunked uploads ki complexity
common_mistakes: Image config ka User field setuid se implement karke secure samajhna
Build pehle banana jab shared store nahi
zstd ko gzip.open se padhne ki koshish
follow_up_questions: Entrypoint aur Cmd ka merge exact docker rules se kaise hota hai?
Upper dir ko layer tar mein badalte waqt opaque directories kaise detect karoge?
Kaunsa step pehle security track ko maangta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Har feature ke saath trust surface badhta hai. Config use karna sasta aur safe; User field security track ke bina misleading. Build ke liye upper->layer conversion ka sabse mushkil hissa whiteout/opaque conversion aur reproducibility (mtimes) hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: 1) Config Env mein PATH missing -> commands 127. 2) Cmd override galat merge -> galat process. 3) zstd layer par aaj -> clear RegistryError, kal decoder bug -> diff_id mismatch (jo verification pakdega). 4) Build mein opaque dir miss -> deleted files wapas. 5) Push mein partial upload -> registry mein orphan uploads.
advanced.alternatives: Existing tools reuse: skopeo/umoci for image ops, buildkit for builds, containerd for store; minibox ko sirf runtime (runc jaisa) rehne dena aur OCI runtime-spec config.json input lena.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x users: shared store aur gc pehle chahiye. 100x: registry mirror, lazy pulling, aur build cache (layer reuse by content). Runtime side (namespaces/cgroups) ka scale pe asar kam; image side ka zyada.
advanced.production_improvements: OCI runtime-spec config.json generation (image config -> runtime spec), conformance tests against runc behaviour, image signing in push, reproducible builds (fixed mtimes jaise tests ka make_tar 1_700_000_000 use karta hai), aur security track (userns, caps, seccomp) ko image User support se pehle.

question: minibox implements the registry pull itself with stdlib urllib, hashlib and tarfile (about 250 lines) instead of shelling out to skopeo/umoci or using containerd. Defend or challenge that decision for a learning runtime and for production.
answer_hinglish:
PLAN.md decision: Python 3.12, zero third-party runtime dependencies, aur 'The registry pull fit in stdlib (about 250 lines), so the alpine minirootfs fallback was not needed.'

DEFEND (learning runtime ke liye):
- Har step visible aur testable: 401 challenge, token, index, platform, digest, diff_id, whiteouts, tar safety -- sab apne code mein, sab unit tested (FakeRegistry, fixture tars), aur mutations M20-M29 mein 10 mein se 10 pakde gaye. skopeo call karte toh yeh sab ek black box hota.
- Seams saaf: injectable fetch se network ke bina poora flow test; Windows par bhi 140 unit tests chalte hain.
- Real bugs khud discover hue jo tool use karne par kabhi nazar nahi aate: tarfile ka 'tar' filter /tmp 1777 ko 0755 bana deta (M28), urllib redirects par token forward karta agar normal header hota (M29), whiteout ordering (M25).
- Real Docker Hub par kaam karta hai: alpine:3.20 arm64, 1 layer, 4092319 bytes, 517 entries, about 4 s.

CHALLENGE (production ke liye):
- Missing pieces jo mature tools mein hain: retries/backoff, resumable downloads, token refresh, private registry credentials, zstd, shared content store + gc, signature verification, parallel downloads, mirrors, proxy config.
- Security-sensitive parsing (tar as root) ko battle-tested code (containerd archive, umoci) mein chhodna behtar; hamare checks (clean_member_path, _inside realpath) achhe hain lekin TOCTOU-free nahi (openat2 nahi).
- Maintenance: registry spec evolve hota hai (referrers API, artifacts), har change hamein track karna padega.

Verdict: learning runtime ke liye stdlib implementation sahi choice thi -- goal 'explain from code you wrote' tha aur tests ne woh prove kiya. Production mein main recommend karunga image handling containerd (ya skopeo + umoci) ko dena, aur apna runtime OCI runtime-spec bundle (rootfs + config.json) consume kare -- jaise runc karta hai. Runtime aur image management alag concerns hain.
why_needed: Build vs buy senior engineering ka core judgement hai, aur yahan dono side ke concrete evidence hain.
real_world_analogy: Driving seekhne ke liye manual gear car (sab control aapke haath, har galti dikhti hai); roz office jaane ke liye automatic car with ABS (mature, safe, kam control).
how_it_works: Decision factors: goal (learning vs operating), test evidence, missing features list, security surface, maintenance cost.
in_this_project: PLAN.md Decisions (Python stdlib, images), registry.py (280 lines incl. docs), image.py, tests/unit/test_registry.py, README mutation table M20-M29 aur NOT-done list.

Zero dependencies, kahin bhi unit tests
Bugs khud discover aur document hue
disadvantages: Production features ki lambi missing list
Security-critical parsing khud maintain karna
Spec evolution track karna
common_mistakes: 'Humne likha toh production-ready hai' maan lena
Learning goal ke liye bhi black-box tool use karke samajh kho dena
Runtime aur image management ko ek hi component mein jodte jaana

Runtime ko OCI bundle consume karne wala banana -- minibox mein kya badlega?
Tar extraction ko sandbox mein kaise chalaoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Stdlib implementation = control, visibility, testability; mature tools = features, hardening, ecosystem compatibility. Middle path: apna thin client sirf learning ke liye, production mein containerd API ya skopeo/umoci, aur runtime sirf OCI bundle se kaam kare.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Apne puller ke saath: Docker Hub rate limit (429) par koi backoff nahi, token expiry on bade layers, private registries unsupported, zstd images fail. Tool ke saath: version drift, external binary missing, black-box errors debug karna mushkil.

advanced.production_improvements: Agar apna puller rakhna hi ho: retries/backoff, Range resume, credential helpers, zstd, signature verification, openat2-based extraction, fuzzing of tar handling, aur conformance tests against the OCI distribution spec.
